paper_title: Decoupling Disease, Covariates, and Individual Variability: A Unified Disentanglement Framework
core_problem: Deep learning models struggle to disentangle disease-specific pathological signals from confounding covariates (e.g., age, gender, acquisition site, education level, scanner type) and individual variations in medical image classification.
methodology_summary: A generalized Medical Imaging Disentanglement Learning (MedIDL) framework that maps image features into three mutually orthogonal latent spaces using specialized heads: a disease classification head (supervised loss), a covariate-alignment head (cross-subject similarity matching), and a Gaussian head (absorbing individual variations).
empirical_results: MedIDL outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and self-supervised classification methods in accuracy across all datasets. Association analyses confirm successful isolation of target-specific latent representations, and gradient-based interpretability localizes pathognomonic patterns aligning with clinical literature.
explicit_limitations: The provided text mentions overcoming limitations by proposing MedIDL, but does not explicitly list inherent limitations of the proposed framework itself, only the challenge it addresses.
